system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:39 UTC, ivy.chen opened C:\Users\ivy.chen\Downloads\Statement.docm in Word.
About one second later, Word spawned PowerShell under ivy.chen's account. PowerShell used -nop, -w hidden, and an encoded command.
That PowerShell process connected through the proxy and retrieved u.ps1 from raw.githubusercontent.com; the proxy recorded an HTTP 200 response.
PowerShell then spawned rundll32 to invoke C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init. The process was recorded starting and later exiting.
The Word-to-hidden-PowerShell-to-download-to-rundll32 sequence is strongly indicative of malicious execution, rather than an ordinary interactive PowerShell window.

A separate PowerShell process ran earlier at 13:31 as SYSTEM, launched by taskeng.exe with the command to run C:\Scripts\service-health.ps1; it is distinct in time, user, parent, and command from the 13:44 activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the downloaded script URL and HTTP 200 status, but do not include the script contents.
The records show rundll32 invoked svchelper.dll, but do not provide the DLL's contents, hash, creation event, or a direct record confirming what its Init export did.
The available process and network records do not establish whether the activity created persistence or resulted in further compromise.
claims_not_established: Who authored or delivered Statement.docm, or whether ivy.chen intentionally opened it.
What code was in u.ps1 or svchelper.dll, and whether the requested GitHub content was authorized.
Whether the payload successfully completed its intended actions, persisted, stole data, or affected other systems.
Whether the PowerShell event matched the user's approximate report time; the recorded suspicious launch occurred at 13:44:40 UTC.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect Statement.docm, u.ps1, and svchelper.dll, preserving metadata and calculating hashes; examine the document's macros and the downloaded script and DLL.
Obtain endpoint protection detections, quarantine history, and available process, file, registry, and memory telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01 around and after 13:44 UTC.
Retrieve the full proxy response or cached content for the GitHub request and verify the repository, commit, and file against an authorized source.
Investigate the document's origin and the user's activity, and search other hosts for the same file hashes, URLs, process command lines, and related indicators.
